_doc: The S-13 client-repoint inventory: every tracked file carrying an address that MOVES in the
generation-1 -> generation-2 cutover, and what each one is.
This file is DATA for scripts/check-cutover-consumers.sh, which fails when the tree and this
manifest disagree in either direction. It exists because the cutover's realistic failure mode is
not repointing the wrong address - it is repointing 30 of 35 files and shipping the other 5 still
Addresses are matched in FULL (40 hex digits) and CASE-INSENSITIVELY. Both halves are load-bearing;
see docs/CLIENT_REPOINT.md for the two ways an 8-hex case-sensitive grep gets this wrong.
generation2 is null for every entry because nothing is deployed. S-13 repoints; S-14 deploys.
A placeholder here would be the invented data this fleet forbids.

movingAddresses.supersededBy: SPLITS BY CALLER ROLE - see supersededBy on each consumer entry
note: THE ONLY MOVING ADDRESS THAT DOES NOT HAVE ONE TARGET. It splits by what the caller does with
it, and the two halves move in OPPOSITE directions - so a per-consumer `supersededBy` overrides
this entry wherever the answer is not the reader default.
READER (resolves the write-once rootIssuer[R], or asks isClone) -> CloneProvenanceRouter, which
answers across BOTH generations oldest-first. Point a reader at DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 and every
one of the 19 historical roots resolves to address(0), surfacing as an indeterminate
issuer-whitelist pillar rather than an error. The router's isClone is also DELIBERATELY wider -
true for a clone of any registered generation - which is the question a post-cutover provenance
check must ask; a generation-1-only answer reports every genuine generation-2 clone as
NotFactoryDeployed.
WRITER (predictIssuer / createIssuer calldata) -> DogTagIssuerFactoryV2. The router deploys
nothing and owns nothing.
EMITTER ALLOWLIST (the indexer's INDEXER_GENERATIONS.factory) -> DogTagIssuerFactoryV2, and as an
APPEND beside generation 1 rather than a swap. That list is keyed by who SIGNED a log, and the
router emits nothing, so a router address there would silently match no event ever.
Superseded as the authority core. Generation-1 clones keep reading the generation-1 registry
on-chain regardless - a clone pins its registry at initialize with no setter - so this is a
CONSUMER-side repoint only, and generation-1 issuance is unaffected until the C-12 freeze.
The mandatory issuer-whitelist pillar does not yet answer for a generation-2 root: see
docs/ISSUER_V2_OWNERSHIP.md section 8. That is a cutover blocker, not part of this slice.
Its issuerRegistry / sbt / rootIndex are all immutable, so replacing the authority core forces
this redeploy on its own. C-6 must migrate the VERIFY: relayer capabilities BEFORE any client
is repointed here: restrictToWhitelistedRelayers defaults true, so a client on V2 whose relayer
was not migrated gets !verify-wl on every verification.
The discovery anchor. Generation 2 publishes under the NEW discovery key dogtag-levelb/2; the
ARTIFACT key stays dogtag-levelb-artifacts/1 because the artifacts are byte-for-byte identical
and a second identity for them would be a falsehood. See docs/PROTOCOL_REGISTRY_V2.md.
Abandoning the deployed one is free: boundCloneCount() == 0 AND zero logs of any kind at head
303690 on 2026-07-30. Read the log count, not just the counter - setDomainAdmin appoints a key
without writing a binding, so only 'no logs' establishes nothing is stranded.
The clone implementation. DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 identifies it EXACTLY, by
impl.codehash == keccak256(type(DogTagIssuerV2).runtimeCode), so an ABI-shaped impostor is
refused at construction. Carried here because both mobile bundles and the ledger record it.

_doNotMoveDoc: Two live addresses are deliberately REUSED by generation 2 and must not appear in any repoint.
Listing them is the point: they look like they should move and they must not.

reason: profileRoot is per-contract and write-once, so a new SBT has no root for any existing tag and
every existing tag would fail the R == profileRoot(dogTagId) binding. Reuse costs nothing:
minting gates on the SBT's own ISSUER_ROLE, not on the issuer registry, so it is independent
of the authority swap. C-10b must grant that role to the generation-2 issuing signers.
The circuit and the ceremony VK are frozen and unchanged by any of this work.

_consumerClassDoc.runtime-constant: A compiled-in or bundled constant that resolves a live address. Repoint at C-9/C-10.
_consumerClassDoc.service-default: A backend's hard-coded fallback for an env var. Repoint at C-9.
_consumerClassDoc.config-template: .env.example - operator-facing template, read by nobody at runtime. Moves with the code per the captain's standing rule.
_consumerClassDoc.operational-script: A demo/e2e shell script that drives the live chain. Repoint at C-9.
_consumerClassDoc.documentation: A live-address table or runbook. Moves with the code.
_consumerClassDoc.historical-ledger: PRESERVE. The deployment record. AGENTS.md: do not rewrite historical records.
_consumerClassDoc.pinned-fixture: PRESERVE. Pinned to a block; the S-12 fork test REFUSES to run if it disagrees with the fork.
_consumerClassDoc.hermetic-fixture: PRESERVE. A MemChain or mocked-network constant that resolves nothing live. Reusing a real address here is cosmetic.
_consumerClassDoc.inventory-manifest: PRESERVE the generation-1 values. This file itself, which records WHAT MOVED and therefore holds every generation-1 address by design. S-14 fills each `generation2` beside its `generation1`; it never replaces one, or the record of what moved from where is lost.

Declared rather than skipped. An implicit self-exemption is a silent hole in the one check that exists to find silent holes - and this entry was added only because the gate flagged its own manifest the moment it became tracked. Until then the check was passing because git grep cannot see an untracked file, which is a check passing by not running.

_elidedDoc: Files that reference a moving address ONLY in elided prose form (0xED20269E...), so a full-address
grep cannot see them. They still need a human edit at cutover. They are listed rather than matched
because widening the grep to 8-hex prefixes produces false positives - see docs/CLIENT_REPOINT.md.
